findings.text: rule() returns only the first rule for a selector, so T-29 and the A2 checks do not see a later rule that overrides it. Appending 'h2 { font-family: sans-serif; } body { background: white; }' leaves them green. Direct removals and value changes are all caught, so this is a limit of the regression guard and does not fail A4.

debt.drag: A later unit's stylesheet addition could override the look or the targets without any test going red; only the walk would see it.

reasons: A1 met: verified in Chromium at 360x640 on every page, including b1's long URL and long typed values. The builder's report does not cover all of this (see note).
A2 met: keyboard paths, the ink focus ring and 44px targets all verified in the browser.

A3 not met in one narrow respect: the markup is right on every page I rendered, but test/access.test.js does not prove it on the empty-shelf page, which the clause and a standing item both cover. This is the only blocker.

A4 met: T-29 reddens on five direct mutations. The look holds in screenshots: no card grid, app-store chrome or template feel. Hand lettering could not be seen here because the fonts are absent, and the builder reports that honestly; the V-11 lettering judgement stays with the walk.
The mutation-smoke survivor on W-1 is acceptable: the look rules predate this unit, and the test does fail when those rules are broken.
No non-goal was breached: no new copy, palette, font, script or dependency. The full suite passes 83/83, and I-20 and I-21 remain future work for settings-file.
